literature.title: ResearchAgent: Iterative Research Idea Generation over Scientific Literature with Large Language Models
literature.abstract: The pace of scientific research, vital for improving human life, is complex, slow, and needs specialized expertise. Meanwhile, novel, impactful research often stems from both a deep understanding of prior work, and a cross-pollination of ideas across domains and fields. To enhance the productivity of researchers, we propose ResearchAgent, which leverages the encyclopedic knowledge and linguistic reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to assist them in their work. This system automatically defines novel problems, proposes methods and designs experiments, while iteratively refining them based on the feedback from collaborative LLM-powered reviewing agents. Specifically, starting with a core scientific paper, ResearchAgent is augmented not only with relevant publications by connecting information over an academic graph but also entities retrieved from a knowledge store derived from shared underlying concepts mined across numerous papers. Then, mimicking a scientific approach to improving ideas with peer discussions, we leverage multiple LLM-based ReviewingAgents that provide reviews and feedback via iterative revision processes. These reviewing agents are instantiated with human preference-aligned LLMs whose criteria for evaluation are elicited from actual human judgments via LLM prompting. We experimentally validate our ResearchAgent on scientific publications across multiple disciplines, showing its effectiveness in generating novel, clear, and valid ideas based on both human and modelbased evaluation results. Our initial foray into AI-mediated scientific research has important implications for the development of future systems aimed at supporting researchers in their ideation and operationalization of novel work1.

literature.title: Literature-Grounded Novelty Assessment of Scientific Ideas
literature.abstract: Automated scientific idea generation systems have made remarkable progress, yet the automatic evaluation of idea novelty remains a critical and underexplored challenge. Manual evaluation of novelty through literature review is labor-intensive, prone to error due to subjectivity, and impractical at scale. To address these issues, we propose the Idea Novelty Checker, an LLM-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework that leverages a two-stage retrieve-then-rerank approach. The Idea Novelty Checker first collects a broad set of relevant papers using keyword and snippet-based retrieval, then refines this collection through embedding-based filtering followed by facet-based LLM re-ranking. It incorporates expert-labeled examples to guide the system in comparing papers for novelty evaluation and in generating literature-grounded reasoning. Our extensive experiments demonstrate that our novelty checker achieves approximately 13% higher agreement than existing approaches. Ablation studies further showcases the importance of the facet-based re-ranker in identifying the most relevant literature for novelty evaluation.

literature.title: Chain of Ideas: Revolutionizing Research Via Novel Idea Development with LLM Agents
literature.abstract: Research ideation is crucial for scientific progress, but the exponential increase in scientific literature makes it challenging to stay updated and identify impactful directions. Recent developments in large language models (LLMs) offer a promising avenue to automate this process. However, existing methods for idea generation either trivially prompt LLMs or expose LLMs to extensive literature without indicating useful information. Inspired by human research processes, we propose a Chain-ofIdeas (CoI) agent, an LLM-based agent that organizes relevant literature in a chain structure to effectively mirror the progressive development in a research domain. This organization helps LLMs better grasp current advancements, thereby improving ideation capabilities. Further, we present Idea Arena, a protocol for evaluating idea-generation methods from different perspectives, which aligns closely with the preferences of human researchers. Experiments show that CoI agent consistently outperforms existing methods and matches human quality in idea generation. Moreover, CoI agent is budgetfriendly, requiring only $0.50 to generate a candidate idea and its experimental design1 .

literature.title: HypER: Literature-grounded Hypothesis Generation and Distillation with Provenance
literature.abstract: Large Language models have demonstrated promising performance in research ideation across scientific domains. Hypothesis development, the process of generating a highly specific declarative statement connecting a research idea with empirical validation, has received relatively less attention. Existing approaches trivially deploy retrieval augmentation and focus only on the quality of the final output ignoring the underlying reasoning process behind ideation. We present HypER (Hypothesis Generation with Explanation and Reasoning), a small language model (SLM) trained for literature-guided reasoning and evidence-based hypothesis generation. HypER is trained in a multi-task setting to discriminate between valid and invalid scientific reasoning chains in presence of controlled distractions. We find that HypER outperforms the base model, distinguishing valid from invalid reasoning chains (+22% average absolute F1), generates better evidence-grounded hypotheses (0.327 vs. 0.305 base model) with high feasibility and impact as judged by human experts (>3.5 on 5-point Likert scale). literature.title: SciMON: Scientific Inspiration Machines Optimized for Novelty
literature.abstract: We explore and enhance the ability of neural language models to generate novel scientific directions grounded in literature. Work on literature-based hypothesis generation has traditionally focused on binary link prediction—severely limiting the expressivity of hypotheses. This line of work also does not focus on optimizing novelty. We take a dramatic departure with a novel setting in which models use as input background contexts (e.g., problems, experimental settings, goals), and output natural language ideas grounded in literature. We present SciMON, a modeling framework that uses retrieval of “inspirations” from past scientific papers, and explicitly optimizes for novelty by iteratively comparing to prior papers and updating idea suggestions until sufficient novelty is achieved. Comprehensive evaluations reveal that GPT-4 tends to generate ideas with overall low technical depth and novelty, while our methods partially mitigate this issue. Our work represents a first step toward evaluating and developing language models that generate new ideas derived from the scientific literature. Code, data, and resources are publicly available for research purposes: https://github.com/eaglew/clbd.

initial_idea.title: Integrating Automated Novelty Checking into Chain-of-Ideas Scientific Generation Frameworks
initial_idea.research_problem: How to dynamically filter and direct multi-step scientific idea generation paths using automated literature-grounded novelty assessment.
initial_idea.research_gap: Current chain-based and iterative LLM ideation frameworks effectively capture progressive domain developments and simulate peer reviews, but they lack real-time integration with rigorous, facet-based novelty checking mechanisms, often resulting in incremental ideas that overlap with existing literature.
initial_idea.methodology: We propose a modular pipeline combining Chain-of-Ideas (CoI) agent generation with an Idea Novelty Checker retrieval-augmented re-ranking module. During each step of the iterative idea evolution chain, candidate generation paths are queried against a vector database of scientific literature using a two-stage retrieve-then-rerank approach. If a candidate idea exhibits high semantic overlap and low facet-level divergence compared to existing papers, the novelty checker injects specific negative constraints and citation gaps into the prompt context, forcing the CoI agent to pivot towards unexplored directions before proceeding to subsequent refinement steps.
initial_idea.expected_contribution: A unified framework that bridges automated literature-grounded novelty checking with multi-step research ideation agents, significantly improving the originality and technical depth of generated scientific proposals without requiring model training.
initial_idea.experimental_setup: We select a benchmark set of 100 recent computer science and NLP problem statements from public conference repositories. We compare three configurations: standard CoI agent generation, a baseline with random literature retrieval augmentation, and our proposed novelty-guided CoI pipeline. Each method generates 3 distinct research proposals per problem statement.
initial_idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate the generated proposals using a dual-pronged approach: (1) Automated novelty scoring using the Idea Novelty Checker framework to measure distance from historical literature embeddings, and (2) Expert-aligned LLM judging protocols (Idea Arena) evaluating feasibility, technical depth, and overall scientific impact.
feasibility_assumptions: API access to frontier language models is available for agentic generation and prompt execution.
Pre-computed academic vector embeddings and retrieval indices from baseline literature sets can be queried locally or via public APIs.
Experiments can be fully executed within a 6-week timeframe using Python orchestration scripts.

final_idea.title: Integrating Automated Facet-Based Novelty Checking into Chain-of-Ideas Scientific Generation Frameworks
final_idea.research_problem: How to dynamically filter and direct multi-step scientific idea generation paths using automated literature-grounded facet novelty assessment while controlling for execution latency, prompt degradation, and logical coherence under strict resource constraints.
final_idea.research_gap: While prior work like SciMON and Chain-of-Ideas (CoI) frameworks structure progressive research domains and optimize for novelty, existing frameworks lack real-time integration with rigorous, facet-based novelty checking mechanisms as proposed by Shahid et al. (2025). Directly applying multi-step retrieval loops risks compounding latency and token costs through unconstrained negative constraints. Furthermore, proxy models or cached vector lookups often miss subtle cross-domain semantic intersections, causing false negatives or superficial keyword avoidance without violating the constraint of no LLM training.
final_idea.methodology: We integrate the Idea Novelty Checker framework with CoI agent generation via a zero-training orchestration pipeline. To address latency bottlenecks without model fine-tuning, we utilize frozen few-shot prompting paired with compressed vector summaries and pre-computed academic embeddings, ensuring intermediate steps retain fine-grained facet awareness. Rather than using restrictive negative prompts that cause text degeneration, we restructure the negative constraint injection mechanism to provide constructive directional scaffolds highlighting open architectural directions. We also incorporate a structural validity filter based on explicit heuristic thresholds to ensure steered pivots preserve technical soundness.
final_idea.expected_contribution: A unified, cost-effective framework bridging automated facet-based novelty checking with multi-step research ideation agents, significantly improving originality and technical depth without expensive runtime reranking loops or model training.
final_idea.experimental_setup: We select a curated benchmark set of 10 high-impact computer science and natural language processing problem statements to fit within a 6-week timeframe and single 12GB GPU constraint. We compare four configurations: standard CoI agent generation, random retrieval augmentation, SciMON baseline, and our proposed novelty-guided CoI pipeline. Each method generates 3 distinct proposals per problem statement, incorporating a systematic ablation isolating the performance delta introduced by prompt-based intermediate checking and constructive directional scaffolds.
final_idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate proposals using a dual-pronged approach: (1) Automated facet novelty scoring using the Idea Novelty Checker framework to measure distance from historical literature embeddings alongside quantitative agreement thresholds, and (2) Expert-aligned LLM judging protocols (Idea Arena) evaluating feasibility, technical depth, and overall scientific impact.
feasibility_assumptions: API access to frontier language models is available for agentic generation and prompt execution.
Pre-computed academic vector embeddings and retrieval indices from baseline literature sets can be queried locally using Python orchestration scripts with minimal memory overhead.

Experiments can be fully executed within a 6-week timeframe by restricting the evaluation subset to 10 problem statements and enforcing early stopping criteria for novelty feedback loops to avoid infinite generation cycles.

review.explanation: The proposal aims to integrate an automated novelty checking mechanism into a chain-of-ideas generation framework. While the specific components—namely Chain-of-Ideas (CoI) agent generation and the Idea Novelty Checker—are powerful individual contributions from recent literature, combining them into an iterative retrieval-and-pivoting loop closely mirrors existing work like SciMON which iteratively optimizes for novelty by comparing generated ideas against prior papers.
problems: The core idea of iteratively refining generated research ideas against retrieved literature to optimize novelty has already been explored in systems like SciMON.
The novelty check relies on embedding-based filtering and LLM re-ranking during generation loops, which can introduce significant latency and token cost overheads across multi-step chain execution.
The distinction between injecting negative constraints from a facet-based novelty checker versus existing iterative reflection loops is incremental rather than a fundamental architectural shift.
improvements: Clearly delineate how the proposed 'Idea Novelty Checker' module differs structurally and functionally from the novelty-optimization feedback loops in SciMON and ResearchAgent.

Introduce a lightweight proxy model or cached local vector lookup for intermediate steps to mitigate the compounding latency and API costs of running a two-stage retrieve-then-rerank pipeline at every single chain iteration.

Incorporate a dedicated user study or downstream empirical validation measuring whether the negative constraints genuinely prevent conceptual overlap without degrading the logical coherence or feasibility of the resulting proposals.

Given the constraints of a 6-week timeframe, 1 consumer GPU or API access, and no model training, the framework is largely feasible because it relies on existing frozen frontier LLMs and modular retrieval/re-ranking pipelines rather than heavy model fine-tuning. However, running multi-step agentic generation with frequent retrieve-then-rerank loops across a large literature vector database for 100 benchmark problem statements with multiple configurations will incur significant API latency and token costs.

Dependence on external frontier model rate limits and stability during multi-agent execution.

Implement local lightweight embedding models and pre-computed vector indices for the retrieval stage to minimize external API dependencies and latency.
Introduce early stopping criteria in the iterative chain-of-ideas evolution steps to cap the maximum number of novelty-checking feedback loops per idea.

review.explanation: The proposal presents a well-structured and highly clear framework for integrating automated novelty checking into chain-of-ideas generation paths. The operational definitions are precise, relying on known components such as Chain-of-Ideas and Idea Novelty Checkers, and the text flows logically from problem identification to methodology and evaluation.
problems: The feedback loop where negative constraints and citation gaps are injected into the prompt context lacks a detailed explanation of token budget management and how long contexts are handled across multiple iterations.
The baseline comparisons include standard CoI and random retrieval, but do not explicitly contrast against iterative novelty-optimization strategies like SciMON.
The dual-pronged evaluation relies heavily on an LLM-based judge (Idea Arena), which might introduce bias toward models with similar stylistic preferences.
improvements: Define a clear threshold or convergence criterion for when an idea is considered sufficiently novel to stop the iterative chain refinement.
Include SciMON or a similar iterative novelty-guided generation framework as an explicit baseline in the experimental setup.
Provide more detail on the exact structure of the negative constraints injected into the prompt and how they prevent semantic loops.

review.explanation: The proposal aims to integrate an automated novelty checker into a Chain-of-Ideas (CoI) agentic generation pipeline to prevent incremental ideas by penalizing semantic overlap and injecting negative constraints. While the system design is clear, the core mechanism relies heavily on prompt engineering tricks (negative constraints and citation gaps) to steer frozen LLMs, which often leads to degradation in logical coherence, technical depth, or hallucinated novelty. Furthermore, the novelty-guided mechanism heavily overlaps with existing work such as SciMON, which similarly optimizes for novelty via iterative retrieval and refinement.
problems: Injecting negative constraints and citation gaps into iterative CoI prompts can destabilize the LLM generation trajectory, resulting in incoherent or practically infeasible research ideas.

The proposed method shows limited distinct novelty over prior iterative novelty-optimization frameworks like SciMON, which also iteratively compares candidate directions against historical literature embeddings.

Relying solely on embedding-based filtering and automated LLM re-ranking for novelty checking risks false positives, where genuine paradigm shifts are penalized due to superficial lexical or semantic overlap with unrelated foundational fields.
improvements: Incorporate a structural validity filter alongside the semantic novelty checker to ensure that steered pivots do not compromise the technical soundness or experimental feasibility of the generated proposal.
Provide a detailed cost and latency analysis of running a two-stage retrieve-then-rerank novelty check at every single step of the multi-step Chain-of-Ideas trajectory.
Perform human expert evaluations on the feasibility and technical depth of the generated ideas rather than relying exclusively on automated LLM-as-a-judge protocols.

revised_idea.title: Integrating Automated Facet-Based Novelty Checking into Chain-of-Ideas Scientific Generation Frameworks
revised_idea.research_problem: How to dynamically filter and direct multi-step scientific idea generation paths using automated literature-grounded facet novelty assessment while controlling for execution latency, prompt degradation, and logical coherence under strict resource constraints.
revised_idea.research_gap: While prior work like SciMON and Chain-of-Ideas (CoI) frameworks structure progressive research domains and optimize for novelty, existing frameworks lack real-time integration with rigorous, facet-based novelty checking mechanisms as proposed by Shahid et al. (2025). Directly applying multi-step retrieval loops risks compounding latency and token costs through unconstrained negative constraints. Furthermore, proxy models or cached vector lookups often miss subtle cross-domain semantic intersections, causing false negatives or superficial keyword avoidance without violating the constraint of no LLM training.
revised_idea.methodology: We integrate the Idea Novelty Checker framework with CoI agent generation via a zero-training orchestration pipeline. To address latency bottlenecks without model fine-tuning, we utilize frozen few-shot prompting paired with compressed vector summaries and pre-computed academic embeddings, ensuring intermediate steps retain fine-grained facet awareness. Rather than using restrictive negative prompts that cause text degeneration, we restructure the negative constraint injection mechanism to provide constructive directional scaffolds highlighting open architectural directions. We also incorporate a structural validity filter based on explicit heuristic thresholds to ensure steered pivots preserve technical soundness.
revised_idea.expected_contribution: A unified, cost-effective framework bridging automated facet-based novelty checking with multi-step research ideation agents, significantly improving originality and technical depth without expensive runtime reranking loops or model training.
revised_idea.experimental_setup: We select a curated benchmark set of 10 high-impact computer science and natural language processing problem statements to fit within a 6-week timeframe and single 12GB GPU constraint. We compare four configurations: standard CoI agent generation, random retrieval augmentation, SciMON baseline, and our proposed novelty-guided CoI pipeline. Each method generates 3 distinct proposals per problem statement, incorporating a systematic ablation isolating the performance delta introduced by prompt-based intermediate checking and constructive directional scaffolds.
revised_idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate proposals using a dual-pronged approach: (1) Automated facet novelty scoring using the Idea Novelty Checker framework to measure distance from historical literature embeddings alongside quantitative agreement thresholds, and (2) Expert-aligned LLM judging protocols (Idea Arena) evaluating feasibility, technical depth, and overall scientific impact.
feasibility_assumptions: API access to frontier language models is available for agentic generation and prompt execution.
Pre-computed academic vector embeddings and retrieval indices from baseline literature sets can be queried locally using Python orchestration scripts with minimal memory overhead.

Experiments can be fully executed within a 6-week timeframe by restricting the evaluation subset to 10 problem statements and enforcing early stopping criteria for novelty feedback loops to avoid infinite generation cycles.
